The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is the anodic half reaction of water electrolysis, in which water is oxidized to O2. It is kinetically sluggish, and rutile RuO2 and IrO2 are among the most active known catalysts. In a widely used computational model, the reaction proceeds through four proton-electron transfer steps via adsorbed O, OH and OOH, and the theoretical overpotential is set by the largest free energy step computed from their adsorption energies relative to the standard hydrogen electrode. Because these adsorption energies scale with one another, activity can be plotted on a [volcano plot](/papers/topics/volcano-plot/) against a single descriptor. See also [Adsorption scaling relations](/papers/topics/adsorption-scaling-relations/).

## Polymorph structure as an OER tuning handle (2015)

Xu and Kitchin used this framework on anatase, brookite, columbite and pyrite polymorphs of RuO2, RhO2, IrO2 and PtO2, with adsorption at five-fold coordinatively unsaturated cation sites. O, OH and OOH adsorption energies on the polymorphs fell on the same scaling lines as on rutile, so the polymorphs sit on the same volcano but at different positions. Anatase and columbite IrO2 and brookite RhO2 and PtO2 were predicted to have lower theoretical overpotentials than the rutile forms, and columbite IrO2 was singled out as a synthesis target. The authors present this as a test of whether structural distortions can change activity substantially, not as a complete assessment of any one surface ([Xu 2015](/papers/xu2015a/)). Summary: [xu2015a](/papers/xu2015a/); see also [Oxide polymorphs](/papers/topics/oxide-polymorphs/).

## A common descriptor for OER intermediates on metals and oxides (2013)

Calle-Vallejo and co-workers proposed the number of outer electrons on the active metal as a descriptor for \*O, \*OH and \*OOH adsorption across 3d metals, monoxides and perovskites. Adsorption weakens with more outer electrons along the 3d series and with higher oxidation state for a given metal, giving a predictive adsorption-energy grid. The \*OOH versus \*OH scaling intercept of 3.2 eV that falls out of the grids implies an intrinsic overpotential for ORR-OER electrocatalysis ([Calle-Vallejo et al. 2013](/papers/callevallejo2013/)). Summary: [callevallejo2013](/papers/callevallejo2013/).

## Effect of a linear response Hubbard U on rutile OER trends (2015)

Xu, Rossmeisl and Kitchin recomputed OER intermediates on rutile (110) surfaces with DFT + U. Adding the linear response U weakened binding by roughly 0.2 to 0.4 eV in reaction energy and slid each oxide along the volcano toward the weak-binding side. For the acid-stable oxides the predicted ordering changed from RhO2 \> IrO2 \> PtO2 \> RuO2 at U = 0 to IrO2 \> RhO2 \> RuO2 \> PtO2, closer to the experimental RuO2 ≈ IrO2 \> RhO2 \> PtO2, though no oxide crossed the volcano peak ([Xu et al. 2015](/papers/xu2015/)). Summary: [xu2015](/papers/xu2015/); see also [DFT + U and the Hubbard U](/papers/topics/dft-plus-u/).
